title: Peer-led 30/60/90 Onboarding Sprint and Calibrated Interview Scorecard
body:
PURPOSE
This is a lightweight, peer-led 30/60/90 onboarding sprint combined with a calibrated interview scorecard aimed at reducing time-to-impact for mid-level IC hires (E3-E4) across engineering and product-adjacent roles. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — checklist-first for hiring / interviewers and a rolling buddy schedule for the new hire.

CONTEXT + WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT
- Most existing onboarding decks are top-down. This approach centers early peer involvement: a 2-week micro-rotation with three peer owners to speed cross-team context.
- Includes a short, calibrated interviewer scorecard (behavioral + competency + product sense + communication) to help consistent hiring decisions and faster calibration sessions.

HIGH-LEVEL PLAN
- Pre-boarding (days -10 to 0): paperwork, equipment, initial reading list, team intro messages. People Ops sends welcome kit and assigns first-buddy.
- Week 0 (day 0-7): orientation + role-specific micro-sprint kickoff. Pair with Buddy A (same discipline) every day for 2 hours. Deliverable: small shipping task with mentor sign-off.
- Weeks 1-2 (days 8-14): rotation with Buddy B (cross-functional) and Buddy C (adjacent team) — three paired sessions and 3 async check-ins. Deliverable: 1-page runbook for a common team ops task.
- 30-day checkpoint: demo of the micro-sprint deliverable, feedback from manager and two peers.
- 60-day checkpoint: take ownership of a small feature or process and lead the team demo.
- 90-day checkpoint: graduated to full responsibilities; retention/engagement pulse and first career discussion.

PEER SPRINT SCHEDULE (sample)
- Day -7 to -1: IT/KMS access, Slack invites, Confluence links, running the hello-world repo locally (if applicable).
- Day 0: Intro all-hands, 30-min manager 1:1, 60-min buddy overview.
- Day 1-3: Pair with Buddy A (code/feature walkthrough, tiny bug fix).
- Day 4-7: Pair with Buddy B (product/metrics walkthrough, customer context).
- Week 2: Pair with Buddy C (infra/ops handoff; runbook creation).

CHECKLIST (Pre-boarding -> 30 days)
- Pre-boarding: laptop provisioned, VPN + KMS access, id badge, payroll forms, Slack + Confluence access, onboarding survey sent.
- Day 0: intro email sent to team, calendar blocks for micro-sprint, list of expected deliverables shared.
- By day 7: hello-world task deployed and code signed off, runbook draft started.
- By day 30: runbook finished, deliverable demo scheduled, calendar invite for 30d feedback.

MANAGER ACTIONS (concise)
- Assign three buddies and set expectations (time commitment ~4 hours/week total).
- Add new hire to two correlating projects for exposure.
- Schedule 30/60/90 check-ins in advance.

INTERVIEW SCORECARD — CALIBRATED (single-sheet for interviewers)
Scoring scale: 1-5 (1: strong miss, 3: meets expectation, 5: exceptional). Pass threshold: average >= 3.5 AND no category <= 2.
Categories (short):
  - Technical competence (coding/architecture/problem solving) — weight 35%
  - Product sense & trade-offs (impact orientation, metrics) — weight 25%
  - Collaboration & communication (clarity, empathy) — weight 20%
  - Ownership & learning (bias for action, feedback history) — weight 20%

Quick scoring guidance (bullets for interviewers):
- Technical: ask for specific past examples; ask follow-ups on performance and edge cases; if coding task, note thought process and test coverage.
- Product: ask candidate to decompose a cross-team tradeoff and pick metrics they would own. Look for alignment with Redwood thesis (latency/cost/reliability).
- Collaboration: prefer evidence of cross-functional influence (docs, runbook creation, code reviews).
- Ownership: look for examples of errors caught and how they were fixed; judge growth mindset.

SAMPLE PANEL FOR MID-LEVEL ENGINEER (4 interviews, 50–60 min each)
- Hiring manager (ownership + role fit)
- Peer engineer (system design / coding)
- Product/PM or Solutions Eng (product sense)
- SRE/infra or performance engineer (ops/latency-cost focus)
Panel notes: include one behavioral anchor question at each interview. Use scorecard rubric immediately; add 3-line justification per category in the feedback field.

PASS / FAIL & CALIBRATION FLOW
- After interviews, panel meets for 30 min to share notes and calibrate. People Ops locks the decision only after consensus or manager escalation.
- For marginal candidates (averages 3.2–3.5), schedule a focused follow-up interview (30 min) with a chief stakeholder.

DIVERSITY & INCLUSION CHECKS (practical)
- Ensure at least one panelist is from outside the direct team.
- Use standardized job-related questions; avoid hypothetical culture-fit phrasing.
- Encourage interviewers to document evidence vs opinion.

NEW-HIRE FEEDBACK LOOP
- 7-day pulse (brief Slack survey), 30-day structured feedback call (manager + buddy), 90-day retention pulse + career conversation. Questions to include: onboarding clarity, tooling friction, clarity of role, buddy helpfulness.

OPEN ITEMS / TODOs
- Create a templated 30/60/90 calendar (JIRA-OPS-3421).
- Draft a 1-page interviewer cheat-sheet for product-sense questions.
- Add a short training for buddies: expectations and how to give feedback.

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Testing idea: try pairing new hires with two different senior engineers for the same task and compare ramp-time.
- Consider a lightweight mentor-mentor retro at 45 days to iterate on buddy assignments.

REFERENCES / LINKS
- Onboarding templates (Confluence) — linked in metadata.
- Interview calibration notes: see #interview-calibration in Slack for last quarter notes.

END

This doc is intentionally short-form and meant to be copied into a Drive doc and iterated; use the checklist and scorecard as the actionable pieces that can be pasted into interview invite templates and manager onboarding playbooks.
